paras: The killing of Ernest Williams was the fatal shooting of a Black man in Macon, Georgia, on September 4, 1888, as an excited crowd chased him after he ran from an attempted arrest. Accounts of who fired differed, and at the coroner's inquest the next day three Black witnesses named a white man, Daniel Lucas, as the shooter.

The Savannah Morning News described Williams as a "negro thief and desperado" who had served terms in the chain-gang and penitentiary. That afternoon he became involved in a row in a Fourth street dive, and he ran when Officer Murphy tried to arrest him.

An excited crowd pursued him to the corner of Third and Elm streets, where several shots were fired at him, eight in all. Williams fell, shot through the back, and died almost instantly; a post mortem later found that the ball had passed through his liver. Afterward, according to the first report, two Black men, Samuel Battle and William Williams, tried to incite the gathered crowd to riot, but "prompt action" averted further violence.

The coroner empaneled a jury, which examined the body and adjourned until the next day. On September 5, James Pope, Henry Collins and Robert Colburn testified that Daniel Lucas had run ahead of Officer Johnson, who had fired one shot in the air, and shot Williams from about 30 feet. The paper expected Lucas to be held, but no report of a verdict, indictment or trial was found.

Both reports were Macon dispatches in the Savannah Morning News; no other coverage was found. The first, headlined "A Bad Negro Killed," dwelt on Williams's record, said he "was feared by every one," and called it "almost certain" that the officers had not fired. The next day's item, headlined "Daniel Lucas Apt to be Held for the Killing of Williams," reported the testimony against a white man without comment.

Williams's brother-in-law said a Black man in the crowd who had been Williams's enemy shot him, while the three inquest witnesses named Lucas. The sworn testimony came later and named the shooter, but no verdict was reported.

reader.title: Killing of Ernest Williams
bases: Williams was shot dead while an 'excited crowd' chased him from an attempted arrest, and the inquest testimony named a white civilian in the pursuit, not an officer, as the man who fired (A1, A2).

Both reports come from the same Savannah paper's Macon dispatches and agree that Williams was shot dead in the pursuit, but they disagree on who fired: a Black man in the crowd according to his brother-in-law (A1), or Daniel Lucas, a white man, according to three inquest witnesses (A2).

accounts.label: First Macon dispatch
accounts.gist: Williams was shot while an excited crowd chased him; statements about the shooter conflicted, but it was 'almost certain' the officers did not fire.

accounts.label: Brother-in-law
accounts.gist: A Black man in the pursuing crowd who was Williams's enemy shot him.

accounts.label: Inquest witnesses
accounts.gist: Three Black witnesses testified that Daniel Lucas, a white man, ran ahead of Officer Johnson, who had fired in the air, and shot Williams from about 30 feet.

framing.detail: The first report, headlined 'A Bad Negro Killed', described Williams as a 'negro thief and desperado' who 'was feared by every one' and played down the officers' part.
The follow-up, 'Daniel Lucas Apt to be Held for the Killing of Williams', reported the inquest testimony against a white man without comment.

versions.value: A Black man in the pursuing crowd, an enemy of Williams (brother-in-law's statement)
Daniel Lucas, a white man (three witnesses under oath at the inquest)

conflicts.note: The inquest testimony is later and sworn and names the shooter, so it is the better evidence; no verdict was reported.

versions.value: Officer Johnson was in the pursuit and fired in the air

conflicts.note: These may be two different officers rather than a conflict; neither report names both.

record_check.dossier: 1888-09-04, afternoon (dispatch dated Sept. 4; Sept. 5 is the publication date)
Contested: Daniel Lucas, a white man, per three inquest witnesses; a Black man in the crowd per Williams's brother-in-law

record_check.record: Ernest Williams, a Black thief, was shot dead ... while fleeing arrest by Officer Murphy
record_check.dossier: 'Thief' is the paper's characterization; the inquest testimony that a white man, Daniel Lucas, fired the fatal shot is missing
2 articles in the Savannah Morning News, Sept. 5 and Sept. 6
The paper's framing of the killing; no one claimed to have fired to stop an escape, and the officer reportedly fired only in the air

sources.note: Macon dispatch of Sept. 4, 'A Bad Negro Killed': Williams shot dead fleeing arrest with a crowd at his heels; shooter disputed; inquest adjourned.
quotes: Ernest Williams, a negro thief and desperado, was shot and instantly killed this afternoon while attempting to escape arrest.
He was pursued to the corner of Third and Elm streets by an excited crowd, when several shots were indiscriminately fired at him.
A brother-in-law of the dead negro positively asserted that he was shot by a negro in the pursuing crowd, who had been an enemy of Williams.
